title: Overview — Start Here
useWhen: You are new to MATHALOID Atlas and want to understand what it is, who it serves and why it exists.
summary: What MATHALOID Atlas is, the no-ceiling curriculum promise, the privacy-first principles, and a map of every tab.
plaintext: What is MATHALOID Atlas? MATHALOID Atlas is an open source MIT , privacy first mathematics learning companion that runs entirely in your browser as a single static site. It teaches, drills and guides mathematics from Grade 1 to Matric and beyond into A Levels — no account, no server, no tracking, no ceiling. No ceilings. No limits. Just mathematics. Who it is for Audience What Atlas gives them Learners age 6–19+ Adaptive lessons, games, quizzes and a personal mastery map Parents A safe, offline capable tutor with zero data collection Teachers CAPS / IEB / A Level lenses, exam simulator, classroom drills Contributors A zero dependency codebase that is easy to read, fork and extend The three promises 1. Local first — everything progress, settings, XP lives in your browser's localStorage. The site works from a file, a USB stick or GitHub Pages. 2. Privacy first — the app makes zero network requests after load. The AI tutor Mathaloid Brain runs 100% on device. See Security & privacy security privacy.md . 3. No ceiling — content is organised by curriculum lenses CAPS, IEB, Cambridge A Levels, Global so a curious Grade 4 learner can wander into algebra, and a matriculant can push into calculus.
